docs_considered.role: routine API and unattended preflight contract
decisive_facts: Unattended schedule, API, and webhook runs treat an open routine execution issue as active WIP and coalesce or skip instead of creating another issue.

Routine actionability preflight checks provider backoff, required secrets, blocker owner/state, maintenance cadence, upstream artifact hash, and clean workspace requirements before creating an issue or waking an agent.
Failed preflight finalizes the run as skipped with deterministic evidence, may create or reuse one factory_guard issue, and pauses the routine on the third identical blocker fingerprint.

docs_considered.role: provider routing and context/output economy contract
decisive_facts: OpenCode Go role defaults are the normal route; MiniMax through hermes_minimax is the first automatic degraded lane after quota, rate-limit, auth, billing, or preflight failures.
Post-MiniMax fallbacks require explicit approval flags; without approval, automatic wakes are skipped with provider_degraded_backoff evidence.
Executive, strategic, PM, research, QA, and design work must not be routed to low-intelligence free fallback lanes.
Per-run recovery preserves portable execution config but starts adapter-specific sessions so OpenCode, Hermes, Gemini, Claude, and Codex sessions are not mixed.

docs_considered.role: prompt provenance, provider gate, final disposition, and canary proof contract
decisive_facts: Context ledger entries are created before adapter spawn and store prompt class, component hashes, budget decisions, provider routing metadata, outcomes, receipt paths, and output budget status without storing raw prompt text.
Provider-backed lanes are checked before spawn; auth, billing, quota, rate-limit, and failed preflight are lane-wide degraded failures during the recovery window.
Final disposition is normalized as advanced_vision, maintenance, blocked, noop, or misaligned with nextActionOwner when another party owns the next move.
Flywheel readiness requires issue-linked success, done issue, ledger row, receipt path, passing tests, changed files when applicable, context pack refs, and no hard-stop prompt/provider failure.

docs_considered.role: operator-facing agent, routine, provider, and readiness guidance
decisive_facts: Board operators control agent lifecycle and adapter config; agents can be paused, resumed, budget-paused, or terminated.
Provider reliability is enforced before adapter spawn and recorded with selected lane, failure kind, preflight attempts, prompt hash, and budget status.
Routine conflicts are terminalized instead of stranded; routine actionability skips non-actionable runs and board-owned blockers create reusable factory_guard issues.
Use one ship-captain lane per venture run; Release Gate Reconciler is the seeded Portfolio-OS ship-captain routine.
Run succeeded is not enough; canaryReadiness.readyCount plus listed evidence is the unattended engineering health gate.

docs_considered.role: Portfolio OS cockpit runtime and dispatch-ingest contract
decisive_facts: Portfolio OS remains the truth plane and writes immutable dispatch artifacts; Paperclip ingests them to create companies, projects, workspaces, issues, approvals, and seeded routines.
Dispatch ingest validates repo dossier freshness and semantic-review readiness before creating execution work.
Seeded routines are Dispatch Poller, Run QA Sweep, Evidence Backfill Reconciler, and Release Gate Reconciler, each carrying a paperclip_actionability contract.
Internet Pipes readiness below alpha_ready or factory_ready, or missing stations, keeps work in evidence backfill rather than release-ready state.
Release issues link to launch_execution approval; production deploy remains approval-required.
Paperclip is the governed control plane; Portfolio-OS is the deterministic truth plane.
No workflow or routine is allowed without an explicit success condition and artifact.
Execution is complete only after review, approval, and durable closure artifact, not when code finishes.
Routine families must coalesce or pause under overlap rather than unbounded enqueue.
Daily and weekly cadence requires inspecting ingest health, routing blockers, routine overlap, closure artifacts, approvals, and duplicate descendants.

docs_considered.role: pre-approval migration and target configuration plan
decisive_facts: The document is an approval package, not proof that the live cockpit has already been reconfigured.
Observed pre-plan live state had 4 companies, 60 agents, 73 routines, 26 active routines, 0 active actionability contracts, 0 MiniMax-pinned agents, and 0 company secrets.

Target contract requires every unattended routine to define lane, state, blockerOwner, requiredSecretNames, upstreamArtifactHash, cadenceGroup, minCadenceMinutes, requiresCleanWorkspace, standingIssueKey, and shipCaptain when applicable.

Execution plan after approval is freeze churn, snapshot database, restart current code, attach contracts, collapse duplicates, configure provider routing, configure credential blockers, configure workspace gates, separate maintenance, enforce final dispositions, and verify with bounded live tests.
Non-goals before approval include production deploys, outbound outreach, post-MiniMax paid fallback lanes, deleting audit history, and inferring runtime health from docs or graph artifacts.
MiniMax M3 multi-source ScrapeGraphAI extraction failed with Connection error.
The failed extraction targeted the same unattended factory concepts but produced status ERROR, so it is blocker evidence rather than usable complete graph context.
Dry run succeeded with status OK but only used docs/api/routines.md and returned dry_run true.
This receipt proves the ScrapeGraph path could execute a dry run, not that multi-source operating context was extracted.

current_contracts: Portfolio OS is the canonical truth plane for frozen selections, snapshots, scaffolds, and dispatch artifacts; Paperclip is the governed control plane for orchestration, review, approvals, and company-scoped execution.
Unattended routine runs must pass actionability preflight before issue creation or agent wake.
Open routine execution issues count as active WIP for unattended sources; routine families must coalesce, skip, or pause rather than enqueue duplicates.
Non-actionable runs are finalized as skipped with paperclipActionabilityPreflight evidence, not converted into speculative agent work.
Board-owned, credential, workspace, provider, and human-owned blockers create or reuse deterministic standing guard/lane issues.
The third consecutive identical blocker fingerprint pauses the routine to suppress duplicate loops.

Provider routing uses OpenCode Go role defaults first, MiniMax through hermes_minimax as the first automatic degraded lane, and a hard stop after MiniMax unless explicit post-MiniMax approval is present.
Model-access failures may rotate models inside a lane; auth, billing, quota, rate-limit, and preflight failures stall the lane during the degraded window.
Executive and strategic work must not use low-intelligence free fallback lanes.
Release, QA, deploy, ship, and outreach lanes require clean workspace classification before wake.
Deploy and outreach lanes require company secrets; missing secrets are board-owned blockers and suppress repeated wakes.
Maintenance and governance routines must run at lower cadence and not compete with release, QA, deploy, customer-signal, or distribution lanes.
Every final agent result should include finalDisposition and nextActionOwner when follow-up belongs elsewhere.
Readiness is proven by context-ledger-backed canaries with issue closure, receipt paths, test evidence, changed-file evidence when applicable, context pack refs, and provider routing evidence.
Release Gate Reconciler is the single ship-captain lane for a Portfolio-OS venture run; Dispatch Poller, QA, and Evidence Backfill feed it.
Merge/release and production deploy remain approval-gated; live cockpit mutation requires board/operator approval.
guardrails: Treat docs/plans/unattended-factory-configuration-plan.md as an approval package, not as a receipt that live mutation occurred.
Do not infer runtime health from docs, graph artifacts, or dry-run receipts; require a fresh live guard receipt after restart.
Do not delete historical issues, comments, runs, logs, or audit evidence when collapsing duplicate routine families.
Do not run more agents to rediscover a known blocker; encode known blockers as deterministic state and standing issues.
Do not dispatch release-ready work when Internet Pipes readiness is below alpha_ready/factory_ready or missing stations remain.
Do not enable post-MiniMax paid or subscription fallback lanes without explicit approval flags.
Do not route executive, strategic, PM, research, QA, or design work to weak free fallback lanes.
Do not create deploy/outreach wakes when required secrets are missing.
Do not let governance, drift, skill sync, health, or graph refresh lanes crowd out product execution, release, QA, deploy, customer-signal, or distribution lanes.
Do not treat task completion or run succeeded as sufficient factory health without canary readiness evidence.
Do not mix adapter sessions across fallback lanes.
Cross-company actions must use board-capable authority or fail loudly with a blocking artifact.
configuration_requirements: Attach paperclip_actionability to every active unattended routine.
For each routine set lane, state, blockerOwner, requiredSecretNames, upstreamArtifactHash, cadenceGroup, minCadenceMinutes, requiresCleanWorkspace, standingIssueKey, and shipCaptain where applicable.

Convert duplicate Dispatch Poller, Release Gate, Run QA, Evidence Backfill, QA Gate, Release Readiness, and Operating Contract Drift loops into standing lane issues keyed by company, run id, lane, and blocker class.
Set Release Gate Reconciler as the only ship-captain routine per venture run.
Keep OpenCode Go role defaults as normal routing and configure MiniMax as the first automatic degraded lane through hermes_minimax.
Keep post-MiniMax fallbacks disabled unless explicit approval flags are set.
Create or reuse provider-capacity guard issues when degraded provider state is known.
Create board-owned factory_guard issues for LeadForge Fly.io deploy credentials and YT-Synth social/email distribution credentials.
Add requiredSecretNames to deploy, outreach, and distribution routines and skip them until secrets exist.
Enable dirty-workspace classification for QA, release, deploy, ship, and outreach lanes.
Create one cleanup issue per affected company/workspace and suppress release/QA polling until cleanup is done.
Move operating-contract drift, skill sync, health checks, and graph refresh to lower-frequency maintenance cadence.
Require local adapter prompts and finalization to emit finalDisposition and nextActionOwner when applicable.

Verify live migration with one deterministic skip per blocker class, one ready lane with issue-linked context-ledger evidence, duplicate suppression at the fingerprint threshold, and flywheel-health canary readiness.

blockers_and_owners.blocker: Live cockpit database reportedly has active routines without paperclip_actionability contracts.
Live server/runtime drift cannot be proven from docs; plan reports port/config divergence and process predating actionability implementation.
LeadForge deploy cannot proceed until Fly.io token exists as a company secret.
YT-Synth distribution and outreach cannot proceed until social/email credentials exist as company secrets.
OpenCode/Hermes quota, auth, billing, rate-limit, or preflight failures require MiniMax-first degraded routing and skip evidence when recovery is outside approval boundary.
Post-MiniMax fallback lanes are blocked unless explicit approval flags are set.
Dirty release, QA, deploy, ship, or outreach workspaces must be classified and cleaned before wake.
Duplicate routine families and open routine WIP must be collapsed into standing lane issues rather than new wakes.
agency-swarm lacks an approved unattended execution mandate and should remain paused/archive by default.
MiniMax-backed ScrapeGraphAI multi-source extraction failed with Connection error.
Missing finalDisposition or nextActionOwner makes downstream reporting infer conservative defaults and should be treated as a configuration defect.
Cross-company route-to-existing-venture actions require board-capable authority or must fail with a blocking artifact.

viability_assessment.recommendation: Proceed with unattended factory reconfiguration only after approval to pause scheduled churn, snapshot the database, restart current code, and mutate live routines.
viability_assessment.reason: The docs define a coherent target contract, but the plan explicitly says live cockpit state has not yet been reconfigured and needs approval before mutation.

viability_assessment.recommendation: Attach actionability contracts to active routines and encode blockers as standing issues.
viability_assessment.reason: Routine API and operator docs support deterministic preflight skip evidence, factory_guard reuse, blocker ownership, duplicate fingerprint pause, and clean workspace gates.

viability_assessment.recommendation: Use MiniMax-first degraded provider recovery and stop after MiniMax by default.
viability_assessment.reason: Provider docs define MiniMax as the automatic recovery lane and require explicit flags for later fallbacks.

viability_assessment.recommendation: Enable deploy/outreach/distribution lanes only after required secrets exist.
viability_assessment.reason: LeadForge Fly.io and YT-Synth social/email credentials are explicitly required and reported as missing in the plan.

viability_assessment.recommendation: Collapse duplicate pollers and reconcilers into standing lane issues while preserving history.
viability_assessment.reason: Routine concurrency, WIP recognition, duplicate fingerprint pause, and plan migration steps all support suppression without deleting audit evidence.

viability_assessment.recommendation: Use Release Gate Reconciler as the ship-captain lane for venture runs.
viability_assessment.reason: Portfolio cockpit and managing-agents docs both name Release Gate Reconciler as the seeded ship-captain lane fed by poller, QA, and evidence lanes.

viability_assessment.recommendation: Declare factory readiness only from flywheel canary evidence, not successful run counts.
viability_assessment.reason: Context ledger and managing-agents docs define a concrete readiness gate with issue closure, receipt, tests, changed files, context packs, and provider evidence.

viability_assessment.recommendation: Keep agency-swarm paused/archive unless a concrete execution mandate and credentials are approved.
viability_assessment.reason: The plan classifies agency-swarm as lacking a real execution mandate by default.

viability_assessment.recommendation: Use this native OpenAI/Codex extraction as replacement graph context for the failed MiniMax ScrapeGraphAI pass.
